overview: This report covers 27 unseen announcements: 11 HIGH PRIORITY, 8 RELATED / POSSIBLY INTERESTING, and 8 LOW PRIORITY. Central themes include entropy realization for amenable actions, dimension and overlap phenomena for self-similar measures, equicontinuous factors of semigroup actions, symbolic numeration, and structural restrictions on group actions. Related papers address smooth rigidity, universal approximation of dynamics, hyperbolic trace formulas, stochastic ergodicity, and symmetry in nonlinear systems. Claims are restricted to the supplied abstracts; unspecified hypotheses and formulas, conditional applications, and source-notation limitations are identified explicitly.

paper.title: A family of Hurwitz polynomial vector fields in $\mathbb{R}^3$ having non-constant periodic orbits
paper.abstract: We construct a two-parameter family of polynomial vector fields in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and prove that, on a nonempty open set of parameter values, every member of the family is Hurwitz and possesses two non-constant periodic orbits, one of saddle type and one attracting. This answers Problem 19 in Gasull's list of open problems on low-dimensional dynamical systems concerning the existence of non-constant periodic orbits in Hurwitz smooth vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^3$. This also provides counterexamples to the expected non-existence of non-constant periodic orbits for Hurwitz polynomial vector fields; a question that arose from the first counterexamples to the Markus-Yamabe conjecture in the late 1990s and that was stated by Meisters in his featured MathSciNet review of the Bernat-Llibre counterexample.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is periodic-orbit constructions for polynomial vector fields, with no central entropy, dimension, symbolic, or group-action theme stated.

paper.title: Extrapolating escape dynamics from non-escaping trajectories in Hamiltonian systems
paper.abstract: Hamiltonian systems exhibit rich dynamical behaviors, among which escape is a typical phenomenon. Below the escape threshold, trajectories initiated inside the central potential well remain bounded. Once the energy exceeds this threshold, and the initial conditions lie within the escape basin, the system eventually evolves along unbounded orbits toward infinity. Predicting the escape dynamics is important for understanding the evolution of these systems. In this study, we employ the next-generation reservoir computing framework, a powerful machine learning architecture widely used in dynamical prediction, to address this challenging issue. To capture the intrinsic features of the system, we train the model using data from multiple energy values. Numerical experiments on two Hamiltonian systems show that, with only three time series as training data, each corresponding to an energy value below the escape threshold, the model is capable of not only predicting the escape threshold itself, but also reliably predicting the structure of the escape channels. As a primary contribution of this work, these findings demonstrate that escape dynamics can be inferred from subcritical data alone in the two systems studied, offering a promising paradigm for data-driven studies of Hamiltonian systems.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is numerical machine-learning prediction of Hamiltonian escape, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Unified Relative Orbital Element Framework for Eccentric Formation Flying
paper.abstract: Quasi-nonsingular relative orbital elements (qnsROE) are among the most widely used state representations for formation flying and rendezvous in near-circular inclined orbits. They admit closed-form perturbed state transition matrices (STMs) and a direct geometric mapping, which underpins eccentricity/inclination (E/I)-vector separation for passive safety. Existing eccentric extensions of the qnsROE resolve this geometry in the radial--tangential--normal frame, where a residual semimajor-axis difference makes the E/I separation margin phase dependent. This paper introduces eccentric ROE that reduce to the qnsROE as \(e\to0\) and whose first-order geometry is resolved in the velocity--normal--binormal (VNB) frame, where the secular drift is confined to the velocity direction. Their first-order position and velocity maps yield a closed-form, phase-independent binormal--normal separation bound with an explicit margin for semimajor-axis residuals. Closed-form Keplerian and secular-\(J_2\) STMs and a decoupled impulsive control input matrix are derived for the same elements, and the elements are recovered as the physically normalized integration constants of the Cartesian equations of relative motion in the VNB frame. Together, these results provide a unified ROE framework for formation flying in general elliptic orbits.

analysis.relevance_note: The work develops orbital representations and control tools for spacecraft formation flying.

paper.title: Typical expansive measures for infinite-dimensional maps
paper.abstract: A classical theorem by Ma\~n\'e states that compact metric spaces admitting expansive homeomorphisms must be finite-dimensional. It is a natural question, raised by Morales and Sirvent, whether this dimensional constraint extends to the measure-theoretic notion of expansiveness. In this paper, we answer this question in the negative. We prove that the shift map on the Hilbert cube is expansive with respect to the product Lebesgue measure. Furthermore, we establish a general sufficient condition: any homeomorphism admitting a full-support expansive measure is densely measure-expansive. As a consequence, we show that the set of expansive and topologically stable measures for the shift map contains a dense $G_\delta$ subset, revealing a rich measure-theoretic structure despite the infinite dimensionality of the phase space.

analysis.relevance_note: Measure expansiveness, topological stability, and infinite-dimensional phase spaces directly match the topological dynamics profile.
analysis.tldr: The Hilbert-cube shift is expansive for product Lebesgue measure, despite the infinite-dimensional phase space. The authors also obtain a dense set of measures with expansiveness and topological stability.
analysis.problem: Determine whether the finite-dimensional restriction for expansive homeomorphisms extends to measure-theoretic expansiveness.
analysis.main_result: The authors prove expansiveness of the Hilbert-cube shift with respect to product Lebesgue measure. More generally, a homeomorphism admitting a full-support expansive measure is densely measure-expansive. For the shift, the set of expansive and topologically stable measures contains a dense \(G_\delta\) subset. These are statements about expansiveness relative to measures, not a claim that the Hilbert-cube shift is an expansive homeomorphism.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The abstract contrasts measure-theoretic expansiveness with the finite-dimensional constraint for expansive homeomorphisms and answers the stated question of Morales and Sirvent.

paper.title: Strict correlation-dimension drop for quartic Salem Bernoulli convolutions
paper.abstract:
For every quartic Salem number $ eta\in(1,2)$, we prove that the Bernoulli convolution $
u_{ eta^{-1}}$ with equal weights has correlation dimension strictly less than one. In particular, neither of the two corresponding measures has an $L^2$ density. We relate correlation dimension to exact collision probabilities and express these probabilities as positive integrals over a four-dimensional torus associated with the defining polynomial. The unit-circle conjugates produce a persistent oscillatory term; using carefully chosen return times of the corresponding rotation, we take differences that make this term small while controlling the length and cost of the resulting configurations. Many well-separated placements of these configurations then give a collision probability above the critical scale, which yields the strict dimension drop. The qualitative argument is independent of the computer-assisted estimates. Separate computer-assisted arguments give \[ 0.99999<D_2(
u_{ eta_1^{-1}})<1-10^{-65}, \qquad 0.99999<D_2(
u_{ eta_2^{-1}})<1-10^{-75}, \] where $ eta_1< eta_2$ are the two quartic Salem numbers in $(1,2)$.

analysis.relevance_note: Correlation dimension of Bernoulli convolutions is directly central to fractal geometry and dimension theory.
analysis.tldr: Every equal-weight Bernoulli convolution associated with a quartic Salem number in \((1,2)\) has correlation dimension strictly below one. Separate computer-assisted estimates quantify the very small drop for the two numbers in this interval.
analysis.problem: Establish strict correlation-dimension drop for the stated Salem Bernoulli convolutions and obtain quantitative bounds.
analysis.main_result:
For every quartic Salem number \( eta\in(1,2)\), the authors prove \(D_2(
u_{ eta^{-1}})<1\), hence the measure has no \(L^2\) density. Writing \( eta_1< eta_2\) for the two such numbers, the separate computer-assisted bounds are \(0.99999<D_2(
u_{ eta_1^{-1}})<1-10^{-65}\) and \(0.99999<D_2(
u_{ eta_2^{-1}})<1-10^{-75}\). The qualitative proof is independent of those estimates; the abstract does not assert singularity.
methods: Exact collision probabilities represented as positive integrals over a four-dimensional torus.
Return times of a rotation and differences that suppress an oscillatory term from unit-circle conjugates.
Well-separated placements of configurations; separate computer-assisted quantitative estimates.
analysis.context: The work connects arithmetic properties of Salem numbers with collisions and correlation dimension in Bernoulli convolutions.

paper.title: Ergodic measures of intermediate entropies for amenable group actions with an approximate product property
paper.abstract: We study entropy realization for continuous actions of infinite countable amenable groups. We introduce an approximate product property for amenable group actions that permits a small proportion of tracing mistakes on prescribed pairwise disjoint, sufficiently invariant finite sets. We prove that this property implies entropy-denseness and almost entropy-approximability of every invariant measure. The construction combines zero-entropy exact tilings with a finite-block estimate for the complexity of tracing mistakes. Under asymptotic entropy expansiveness, almost entropy-approximability upgrades to entropy-approximability. For every $0\leq\alpha<h(X,G)$, ergodic measures of entropy $\alpha$ then form a residual subset of the invariant measures whose entropy is at least $\alpha$. In particular, the set of ergodic measure entropies equals $[0,h(X,G)]$.37A35, 37B40, 37B05

analysis.relevance_note: Intermediate entropy realization, amenable actions, and an approximate product property are directly central to the research profile.
analysis.tldr: An approximate product property for infinite countable amenable group actions yields entropy-denseness and almost entropy-approximability. With asymptotic entropy expansiveness, the authors obtain exact entropy realization and a residuality statement.
analysis.problem: Realize prescribed entropies by ergodic measures for continuous amenable group actions.
analysis.main_result: For continuous actions of infinite countable amenable groups, the introduced approximate product property implies entropy-denseness and almost entropy-approximability of every invariant measure. Under asymptotic entropy expansiveness, this becomes entropy-approximability; for every \(0\leq\alpha<h(X,G)\), ergodic measures of entropy \(\alpha\) form a residual subset of the invariant measures with entropy at least \(\alpha\). The abstract additionally states that the set of ergodic entropies equals \([0,h(X,G)]\). Details concerning attainment of the upper endpoint: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Zero-entropy exact tilings.
A finite-block complexity estimate for tracing mistakes on prescribed pairwise disjoint, sufficiently invariant finite sets.
analysis.context: The results link an orbit-tracing property for amenable group actions to approximation of invariant measures and realization of intermediate entropies.

paper.title: Universal Dynamics in a family of Celestial Mechanics models
paper.abstract: Universal maps (maps whose renormalized iterations approximate every map in a given class) are locally generic in several spaces of diffeomorphisms [Bonatti--D\'iaz 2003, Turaev 2015]. In fluid dynamics, steady Euler flows whose Poincar\'e maps are universal are also known to be locally dense [Berger--Florio--PeraltaSalas, 2023]. Motivated by Arnold's vision [Arnold, 1966] that the complexity of orbits in celestial mechanics and that in fluids should be comparable, in the present paper we address the question of the existence of universal maps in celestial mechanics. We give a partial answer by proving a weak, finite-dimensional form of universal dynamics. More concretely, we show that every symplectic embedding of the disk into $\mathbb{R}^2$ can be approximated, with arbitrary precision, by a renormalization of a Poincar\'e map of a restricted planar circular $(n+1)$-body problem, for suitable $n$ and appropriate choice of the masses of the primaries. The proof relies on Gonchenko--Shilnikov--Turaev theory [Turaev 2003, Gonchenko--Turaev--Shilnikov 2007] and requires control of the dynamics near homoclinic tangencies of arbitrarily high order; the techniques developed in [Garrido--Mart\'in--Paradela, 2025] are essential for such control.

analysis.relevance_note: Universal approximation of dynamics and high-order homoclinic tangencies give a substantial connection to orbit complexity, within a celestial-mechanics setting.
analysis.tldr: Every symplectic disk embedding into the plane can be approximated by a renormalized Poincare map from a suitably chosen restricted planar circular many-body problem.
analysis.problem: Find a form of universal dynamics in celestial mechanics.
analysis.main_result: The authors establish a weak, finite-dimensional form of universality: every symplectic embedding of the disk into \(\mathbb{R}^2\) can be approximated with arbitrary precision by a renormalization of a Poincare map of a restricted planar circular \((n+1)\)-body problem, for suitable \(n\) and suitable primary masses. The result permits changing the model parameters; it does not assert that one fixed model approximates every map. The topology of approximation: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Gonchenko-Shilnikov-Turaev theory.
Control near homoclinic tangencies of arbitrarily high order, using the cited techniques of Garrido-Martin-Paradela.
analysis.context: The abstract presents this as a partial answer motivated by comparisons between orbit complexity in celestial mechanics and fluids.

paper.title: When Reducing Transmission Is Not Enough: Carrier Dynamics and Backward Bifurcation in Influenza-Pneumococcal Co-infection
paper.abstract: Bacterial co-infection, particularly with \emph{Streptococcus pneumoniae}, is a major driver of morbidity during influenza epidemics, and this burden falls disproportionately on sub-Saharan Africa, where both pathogens circulate year-round at high levels and pneumococcal carriage remains common and persistent across the region. Yet existing mathematical models rarely track a host's bacterial carriage status jointly with their full influenza history through recovery. We develop a twelve-compartment ODE model that classifies each host by viral status (susceptible, infected, recovered) and bacterial status (susceptible, carrier, actively infected, recovered), allowing carrier-to-active progression to depend on prior influenza exposure. We establish positivity, boundedness, and a positively invariant region, then derive the basic reproduction number $\mathcal{R}_0$ and quasi-endemic equilibria of a single disease, together with invasion reproduction numbers $\mathbf{Inv}^{\mathbf{B}}$ and $\mathbf{Inv}^{\mathbf{V}}$ quantifying each pathogen's ability to invade a population where the other is already endemic. Center-manifold analysis shows that the bacterial subsystem and the full coexistence equilibrium undergo a backward bifurcation precisely when carrier transmission exceeds the carrier's total exit rate, $\beta_c>\kappa_S+\theta+\mu$, so that reducing $\mathcal{R}_0$ below one is not sufficient for elimination, while the viral subsystem bifurcates forward. A global sensitivity analysis (Latin Hypercube Sampling with partial rank correlation coefficients) shows that the viral and bacterial thresholds are governed by largely separate parameters, while the bacterial invasion potential is strongly shaped by viral transmission and recovery, giving a quantitative signature of cross-pathogen synergy.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is epidemic compartment modeling, invasion thresholds, and bifurcation analysis without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Non-rigid disk pseudo-rotations in $C^1$ and $C^{1,\beta}$
paper.abstract: We construct area-preserving irrational pseudo-rotations of the closed disk that fail to be $C^0$-rigid. For every Brjuno rotation number we obtain $C^1$ examples, and they may be chosen arbitrarily $C^1$-close to the rigid rotation with the same rotation number. For $0<\beta<1$, a weighted Brjuno condition gives $C^{1,\beta}$ examples that are arbitrarily close in the $C^{1,\beta}$ topology; this weighted range contains every rotation number with denominator-growth exponent strictly smaller than $1/\beta$ and also some numbers at the critical exponent. For a suitable Brjuno--Liouville rotation number, we also obtain an example whose derivative growth is not bounded by any polynomial.

analysis.relevance_note: Topological rigidity and arithmetic restrictions on disk pseudo-rotations connect closely to smooth and topological dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct area-preserving irrational disk pseudo-rotations that are not rigid in the uniform topology, even arbitrarily close to the corresponding rigid rotations in the stated differentiable topologies.
analysis.problem: Construct non-rigid disk pseudo-rotations with controlled differentiability and rotation arithmetic.
analysis.main_result: For every Brjuno rotation number, there are \(C^1\) area-preserving irrational pseudo-rotations of the closed disk that fail to be \(C^0\)-rigid and are arbitrarily \(C^1\)-close to the corresponding rotation. For \(0<\beta<1\), a weighted Brjuno condition gives analogous \(C^{1,\beta}\) examples; the range includes every rotation number with denominator-growth exponent below \(1/\beta\) and some at the critical exponent. A suitable Brjuno-Liouville rotation number yields an example whose derivative growth is not bounded by any polynomial. The weighted condition's formula: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The constructions distinguish differentiable closeness to a rigid rotation from rigidity of the resulting dynamics.

paper.title: Variational Persistence of Periodic and Quasi-Periodic Orbits in Symmetric $N$-Body Problems
paper.abstract: Many mechanical systems, such as the Newtonian $n$-body system, are invariant under rotations. The rotational symmetry of the system gives rise to two commuting actions: the dynamical action and the action of the symmetry group. In this paper, we exploit this symmetry to construct families of periodic and quasi-periodic trajectories. In the strong-force setting, we extend Montgomery's variational approach to free homotopy classes of curves that are periodic up to a prescribed nontrivial rotation. In the weak-force setting, we establish, under suitable hypotheses, global and local variational persistence results for action minimizers in loop spaces defined by general finite symmetry-group actions under sufficiently small rotations. As applications, we apply these results to the figure-eight orbit, under a numerically supported assumption of strict local minimality, to double choreographic loops with $q$-fold rotation symmetry, and to counter-rotating double choreographic loops in planar $(N+3)$-body problems.

analysis.relevance_note: Finite symmetry actions and homotopy-constrained variational constructions provide an adjacent connection, although the focus is mechanical trajectories.
analysis.tldr: Rotational symmetry yields families of periodic and quasi-periodic trajectories through variational persistence. Some applications remain conditional on hypotheses, including numerically supported local minimality.
analysis.problem: Extend variational orbit constructions to trajectories periodic up to a rotation and study persistence under small rotations.
analysis.main_result: The strong-force result extends Montgomery's variational approach to free homotopy classes of curves periodic up to a prescribed nontrivial rotation. In the weak-force setting, the authors establish global and local persistence for action minimizers in loop spaces defined by general finite symmetry-group actions, under suitable hypotheses and sufficiently small rotations. The figure-eight application assumes strict local minimality supported numerically. Other applications concern double choreographic loops and counter-rotating double choreographies. The remaining suitable hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Montgomery's variational approach in the strong-force setting.
Action minimization in loop spaces defined by finite symmetry-group actions.
analysis.context: The abstract uses the commuting dynamical and rotational-symmetry actions of mechanical systems to construct periodic and quasi-periodic motions.

paper.title: The regionally proximal relation for commutative semigroup actions
paper.abstract: The regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations are fundamental relations in topological dynamics that capture the equicontinuous behavior in a topological dynamical system and its factors. For minimal actions of abelian groups, these relations are known to be equivalence relations and are known to coincide. In this paper, we generalize these facts to semigroup actions: for minimal actions of commutative semigroups, the regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations are equivalence relations and the two coincide. We also develop the machinery of natural extensions for commutative semigroup actions that act by surjections, concluding that the maximal equicontinuous factor of a minimal action of a commutative semigroup is the same as the maximal equicontinuous factor of the group action into which it embeds. We formally verify all of the results in this paper in Lean. The main results are verified in a Palomar submission, and we link to a Github repository containing code for the complete verification.

analysis.relevance_note: Regionally proximal relations, equicontinuous factors, and commutative semigroup actions are directly central to topological dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For minimal commutative semigroup actions, the regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations are equivalence relations and coincide.
analysis.problem: Extend the relation between regional proximality and equicontinuous structure from minimal abelian group actions to commutative semigroups.
analysis.main_result: The authors prove equality of the regionally proximal and equicontinuous structure relations, and their equivalence-relation property, for minimal actions of commutative semigroups. They develop natural extensions for actions by surjections and identify the maximal equicontinuous factor of a minimal semigroup action with that of the group action into which it embeds. The authors report formal verification in Lean; that code has not been inspected for this digest.
methods: Natural extensions for commutative semigroup actions by surjections.
Formal verification in Lean, as reported by the authors.
analysis.context: The results extend the corresponding statements for minimal abelian group actions to the commutative semigroup setting.

paper.title: The Exact Overlaps Conjecture for Self-Similar Measures on the Real Line
paper.abstract: A generalization of the exact overlaps conjecture predicts a formula for the dimension of self-similar measures in terms of the random walk entropy and the Lyapunov exponent. We prove the exact overlaps conjecture and its generalized version in dimension one. The proof relies on a new entropy inequality quantifying the information lost under addition of independent random variables in terms of a quantity averaging variance across scales.

analysis.relevance_note: The exact overlaps problem, self-similar measure dimension, and entropy inequalities are directly central to the research profile.
analysis.tldr: The authors claim proofs of the exact overlaps conjecture and its entropy-based generalization in dimension one, using a new entropy inequality.
analysis.problem: Determine the dimension of self-similar measures on the line in relation to random walk entropy and the Lyapunov exponent.
analysis.main_result: The authors state that they prove both the exact overlaps conjecture and its generalized version in dimension one. Their new entropy inequality quantifies information lost under addition of independent random variables using a quantity that averages variance across scales. The exact dimension formula, detailed hypotheses, and quantitative inequality: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: A new entropy inequality for addition of independent random variables, expressed through variance averaged across scales.
analysis.context: The abstract connects dimension formulas for self-similar measures with random walk entropy, Lyapunov exponents, and multiscale information loss.

paper.title: Finite index extensions of treeable equivalence relations are treeable
paper.abstract: We prove that every countable Borel equivalence relation containing a finite index Borel treeable subequivalence relation is Borel treeable. This answers a long-standing question of Jackson--Kechris--Louveau. Our proof is based on a median subalgebra filtration construction on products of trees, together with an extension of the median graph treeing algorithm of Chen--Poulin--Tao--Tserunyan to certain well-behaved increasing unions.

analysis.relevance_note: Treeability and Borel equivalence relations directly concern the orbit-structure and classification side of the profile.
analysis.tldr: A countable Borel equivalence relation with a finite-index Borel treeable subequivalence relation is itself Borel treeable.
analysis.problem: Determine whether Borel treeability passes from a finite-index subequivalence relation to the full relation.
analysis.main_result: The authors prove that every countable Borel equivalence relation containing a finite-index Borel treeable subequivalence relation is Borel treeable. They identify this as an answer to a question of Jackson-Kechris-Louveau. The result is formulated at the Borel level, without an invariant probability measure hypothesis in the abstract.
methods: A median subalgebra filtration on products of trees.
Extension of the Chen-Poulin-Tao-Tserunyan median graph treeing algorithm to certain well-behaved increasing unions.
analysis.context: The theorem describes stability of a structural property of countable Borel equivalence relations under finite-index extensions.

paper.title: A long time Gutzwiller trace formula for perturbations of Schr\"odinger operators near Anosov energy levels
paper.abstract: Let $P_h$ be a semiclassical pseudodifferential operator on a closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, with principal symbol $p$. We consider perturbations $P_h+h^\alpha Q$, with $0<\alpha\le 1$, where $Q$ is a semiclassical pseudodifferential operator whose symbol oscillates at scale $h^\beta$, with $2\beta <\alpha$. Assuming that the classical dynamics of the unperturbed system on a regular energy surface $p^{-1}(E)$ is hyperbolic, we prove a Gutzwiller trace formula for the perturbed operator that holds up to times of order $|\log h|$. This formula relates the distribution of energy levels of the quantum system near the energy $E$ to the periodic orbits of its classical counterpart. The perturbation $h^\alpha Q$ affects only the phases appearing in the trace formula.

analysis.relevance_note: Hyperbolic classical dynamics and periodic-orbit trace formulas provide a substantial connection to the hyperbolic-dynamics interests.
analysis.tldr: A Gutzwiller trace formula persists up to logarithmic times under the stated oscillatory semiclassical perturbations near a hyperbolic regular energy surface.
analysis.problem: Relate perturbed quantum energy levels to classical periodic orbits over logarithmic time scales.
analysis.main_result: On a closed Riemannian manifold, let \(P_h\) be semiclassical pseudodifferential with principal symbol \(p\). For \(P_h+h^\alpha Q\), where \(0<\alpha\leq1\) and the symbol of \(Q\) oscillates at scale \(h^\beta\) with \(2\beta<\alpha\), the authors assume hyperbolicity of the unperturbed dynamics on the regular surface \(p^{-1}(E)\). They prove a Gutzwiller trace formula up to times of order \(|\log h|\), relating energy levels near \(E\) to classical periodic orbits; the perturbation affects only the formula's phases.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The abstract links semiclassical spectral asymptotics with hyperbolic classical motion and its periodic orbits.

paper.title: Positive-measure intersections of Bedford-McMullen carpets under similitudes
paper.abstract: Let $K=K(n,m,\Gamma)$ be a Bedford-McMullen carpet with $n>m\geq2$ and $1<\#\Gamma<nm$, and let $\mu$ be a self-affine measure on $K$ with strictly positive weights. We prove that if a similitude $f$ satisfies $\mu(K\cap f(K))>0$, then its orthogonal part is diagonal or anti-diagonal. This holds without any arithmetic restrictions on the defining bases. For isometries, we further prove that if $\mu(K\cap f(K))>0$ then $f(K)$ and $K$ differ only by a translation, thereby establishing a strengthened form of the 2010 conjecture of Elekes, Keleti and M\'ath\'e in this planar self-affine context.

analysis.relevance_note: Intersection rigidity of self-affine carpets is directly central to fractal geometry.
analysis.tldr: Positive-measure intersections of a Bedford-McMullen carpet with a similar copy force a diagonal or anti-diagonal orthogonal part. Under an isometry, the two sets must differ only by translation.
analysis.problem: Restrict similitudes and isometries whose images of a Bedford-McMullen carpet meet it in positive self-affine measure.
analysis.main_result: Let \(K=K(n,m,\Gamma)\), with \(n>m\geq2\) and \(1<\#\Gamma<nm\), and let \(\mu\) be a self-affine measure on \(K\) with strictly positive weights. If a similitude \(f\) satisfies \(\mu(K\cap f(K))>0\), its orthogonal part is diagonal or anti-diagonal, with no arithmetic restrictions on the bases. For an isometry with this intersection property, \(f(K)\) and \(K\) differ only by a translation. This is a statement about the image sets, not that \(f\) itself must be a translation.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The authors describe the isometry result as a strengthened form of the Elekes-Keleti-Mathe conjecture in this planar self-affine setting.

paper.title: Unique Ergodicity for Strongly Damped Stochastic Wave Equations under Finite-Rank Pure-Jump L\'{e}vy Forcing
paper.abstract: We study a strongly damped stochastic wave equation on the three-dimensional torus driven by finite-rank pure-jump L\'{e}vy noise obtained from subordinated Brownian motion. Lyapunov estimates and an asymptotic compactness decomposition yield invariant measures, and a small-noise event gives weak irreducibility. To prove uniqueness, we combine conditional Malliavin calculus with terminal observability and estimates for the full variational flow starting from high modes. A control constructed on alternating stopping blocks yields the e-property under a fixed-rank balance condition involving high-mode decay, spectral leakage, and the random clock. Consequently, the invariant measure is unique and ergodic, and the Ces\`aro averages of the transition laws from every initial state converge weakly to it. We verify this condition for sufficiently small positive cubic coefficients at each fixed forcing operator of sufficiently large rank. Under a separate explicit smallness condition, synchronous coupling proves the e-property and weak convergence of the transition laws, without a lower bound on the forcing rank.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant measures and ergodic convergence provide a substantial adjacent connection, although stochastic PDE methods dominate.
analysis.tldr: A strongly damped stochastic wave equation has a unique ergodic invariant measure under a fixed-rank balance condition. A separate smallness condition yields direct convergence of transition laws without a forcing-rank lower bound.
analysis.problem: Establish uniqueness of invariant measures and convergence for a strongly damped wave equation on the three-dimensional torus with finite-rank pure-jump Levy forcing.
analysis.main_result: For noise obtained from subordinated Brownian motion, the authors obtain invariant measures and weak irreducibility. A fixed-rank balance condition involving high-mode decay, spectral leakage, and the random clock yields the e-property, a unique ergodic invariant measure, and weak convergence of Cesaro-averaged transition laws from every initial state. The condition holds for sufficiently small positive cubic coefficients at each fixed forcing operator of sufficiently large rank. Under a separate explicit smallness condition, synchronous coupling yields the e-property and weak convergence of the transition laws themselves without a forcing-rank lower bound. The formulas for these conditions: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Lyapunov estimates, asymptotic compactness, and a small-noise event.
Conditional Malliavin calculus, terminal observability, and full variational-flow estimates from high modes.
Control on alternating stopping blocks; synchronous coupling under the separate smallness condition.
analysis.context: The abstract separates the fixed-rank route to Cesaro convergence from a smallness-based route to convergence without time averaging.

paper.title: Symmetry and Invariant Theory of Quadratic Dynamics over Eight-Dimensional Composition Algebras
paper.abstract: The iteration of $z\mapsto z^2+c$ over the octonions has been drawn for more than thirty years, and it is known that the octonionic Julia sets are bodies of revolution about the imaginary part of the constant. Real eight-dimensional composition algebras, however, are much richer than the octonions: beside the Hurwitz algebras there are the symmetric composition algebras, the para-octonions and the Okubo algebras, which have no unit and whose automorphism groups are $G_2$ and $PSU(3)$ respectively. In this work we study, to our knowledge for the first time, the quadratic dynamics over these algebras, and we do it in an experimental spirit: an atlas of 134 four-dimensional renderings, measured quarter by quarter, suggests the statements, which we then prove and test against new, predicted pictures. We show that the symmetries of the Julia sets of the Okubo algebra are governed by the root decomposition of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ with respect to the plane of $1$ and $i$: for a constant in that plane the continuous symmetry is a maximal torus, which acts by rotations on three root planes and grows to $U(2)$ on the Weyl walls; the automorphism group of the symmetrized product is $PSU(3)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$. We then prove that the Mandelbrot set with seed $0$ of every symmetric composition algebra is the pull-back of a single planar set through the invariants $n(c)$ and $n(c,c\diamond c)$: the tricorn in the compact case, the tricorn and a hyperbolic tricorn in the split case. The result is quite surprising since the para-octonionic and the Okubonic Mandelbrot sets turn out to be the same planar figure saturated by two different groups. Finally, we show that every bilateral map over a symmetric composition algebra is an octonionic quadratic map in disguise, and that at the Petersson angle $\theta=90^\circ$ the dynamics acquires symmetries that do not come from automorphisms.

analysis.relevance_note: Group symmetries of Julia and Mandelbrot sets give an adjacent geometric-dynamics connection; no dimension or entropy result is stated.
analysis.tldr: Experiments motivate proved symmetry and invariant descriptions for quadratic dynamics over symmetric eight-dimensional composition algebras.
analysis.problem: Describe Julia-set symmetries and Mandelbrot sets for quadratic dynamics over para-octonion and Okubo algebras.
analysis.main_result: For Okubo dynamics with the constant in the stated plane of \(1\) and \(i\), the authors describe a maximal-torus continuous symmetry acting on three root planes, enlarging to \(U(2)\) on Weyl walls; the symmetrized product has automorphism group \(PSU(3)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2\). They prove that the seed-zero Mandelbrot set of every symmetric composition algebra is a pull-back through \(n(c)\) and \(n(c,c\diamond c)\): the tricorn in the compact case, and the tricorn together with a hyperbolic tricorn in the split case. paper.title: The full shadow of a polynomial I. The limiting core and the transient set
paper.abstract: The full shadow of a complex polynomial $P$ of degree $d\ge2$ is the closure of all zeros of $(P^n)^{(m)}$, $n\ge1$, $0\le m<dn$. We prove that it consists of a compact connected limiting core containing all roots and critical points of $P$, together with isolated transient zeros, each occurring at only finitely many powers. The core is the Hausdorff limit of the zero sets pooled over all derivative orders as $n\to\infty$ and the support of their limiting normalized root-counting measure. For $m/n\to\alpha\in(0,d)$, we establish weak convergence of normalized root-counting measures and Hausdorff convergence of zero sets to the limiting supports, both stable under coefficient perturbations. We exhibit quartics with infinitely many transients. A bounded operator constructed from polynomial differentiators realizes the full shadow, core, and transients as its spectrum, Fredholm essential spectrum, and discrete spectrum, respectively.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is zeros of derivatives of polynomial powers and their spectral realization, rather than iteration or the central entropy, symbolic, and fractal-dynamics themes.

paper.title: Intrinsic Hutchinson measures and KMS states for iterated function systems with large overlaps
paper.abstract: We study iterated function systems with large overlaps via the Kajiwara-Watatani C*-algebra and its KMS states. Our main contributions are threefold. First, we introduce Markov partitions for iterated function systems and give an algorithm that constructs a finite Markov partition whenever one exists. Second, for contractive systems admitting a finite Markov partition, we construct an intrinsic analogue of the Hutchinson measure that is independent of any labelling or weighting of the maps. It is the unique Borel probability measure satisfying a self-similar integral equation dictated by the set-valued dynamics of the system, and it recovers the Hutchinson measure with uniform weights when the system satisfies the open set condition. Finally, we give a complete classification of KMS states for the gauge action on the Kajiwara-Watatani algebra of every such system. The critical inverse temperature is the exponential growth rate of the intrinsic orbits, which can be strictly smaller than the natural logarithm of the number of maps, and the unique KMS state at this temperature is given by our intrinsic Hutchinson measure. These systems include many with large overlaps not covered by the results of Izumi-Kajiwara-Watatani.

analysis.relevance_note: Markov partitions, overlapping iterated function systems, intrinsic measures, and orbit growth directly match symbolic and fractal dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Contractive iterated function systems with finite Markov partitions admit an intrinsic Hutchinson measure and a complete KMS-state classification, including systems with large overlaps.
analysis.problem: Develop intrinsic measures and KMS-state descriptions for iterated function systems beyond previously covered overlap regimes.

paper.title: Two Answers on Heavy-Ball Dynamics
paper.abstract: We answer two questions about the heavy-ball method on smooth strongly convex functions. The first concerns Polyak's tuning. Its dimension-uniform worst-case exponential rate equals the largest growth factor of an interpolable mixture of rotating geometric sequences, and we determine this factor for every condition number. The optimal mixtures form four algebraic families; the classification combines exact polynomial certificates, a rational parametrization, an exact solution in a quintic number field at the critical three-cycle, and verified interval continuation. Two frequencies suffice, one function in dimension five attains the rate at every horizon, the upper and lower bounds differ by constant factors, and the method converges on the whole class if and only if $\kappa<9+4\sqrt5$, the threshold located by Badithela and Seiler. The second question concerns arbitrary step sizes and momenta, in particular the regions of the parameter plane between the computed Lyapunov and cycle regions. We describe the phase diagram through the angle $\Theta(\omega)$ between the characteristic polynomials of the two extreme quadratics. The method converges when $\Theta(\omega)>\omega/2$, has a $k$-periodic orbit when $\Theta(2\pi j/k)\le\pi/k$, and the remaining regions are rotation-number gaps organized by Farey fractions. A single strict certificate at one growth exponent bounds the rate, so convergence can be certified at the threshold exponent. In the first level of the gaps, fans of Farey fractions accumulating at a resonant endpoint carry periodic orbits with several harmonics, explicit fan-lag inequalities certify convergence, and both behaviors occur in the regions left open before.

analysis.tldr: The authors determine the worst-case exponential rate for Polyak-tuned heavy-ball dynamics and describe convergence and periodic-orbit regions using rotation angles and Farey fractions.
analysis.problem: Determine worst-case convergence rates and resolve parts of the parameter-region structure for heavy-ball dynamics on smooth strongly convex functions.

paper.title: Continuous-Time Critic as a Lyapunov Function: Projected Adaptation and Cart-Pole Stabilization
paper.abstract: We study adaptive stabilization of known control-affine systems by treating the current parameterized critic itself as a Lyapunov candidate. Its total derivative contains a parameter-velocity term that can compensate unfavorable state evolution. A projection onto the intersection of a bounded admissible velocity set and one decay halfspace enforces parameter invariance and Lyapunov decrease simultaneously. We give an exact pointwise feasibility test, a conditional state-stability theorem, and a counterexample showing why a positive critic family containing a stabilizing member does not imply persistent feasibility. A convex endpoint constraint provides a distinct sampled implementation. A generic periodic polynomial-factor critic with a local Riccati anchor is evaluated on a force-limited cart-pole without mechanical-energy features, replay training, waypoints, or controller switching. The frozen controller passes stabilization and numerical decay checks on 600 sampled initial states across two draw sets; 400 matched continuous trajectories also pass. Independent reintegration audits and a conservative local feasibility certificate are distinguished from a global or machine-arithmetic guarantee. Compared with nonlinear model-predictive control, the measured implementation uses less CPU but has higher cost, settling time, and cart travel. The results support a conditional adaptive stabilization mechanism.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is conditional adaptive control and numerical cart-pole stabilization, without a central entropy, symbolic, fractal, or group-action theme.

paper.title: Terminal Blocks of Primes in Pisot Numeration Systems
paper.abstract: We prove a prime number theorem for fixed terminal block words in Pisot integer numeration systems. If the dominant root $\varphi$ is a Pisot number and the characteristic polynomial $P_h$ is its minimal polynomial, every terminal block word of total digit-length $m$ occurs among the primes with asymptotic frequency $\varphi^{-m}$. In the Zeckendorf case this resolves a recent conjecture. The proof converts terminal conditions into Rauzy cylinder windows and then into a linear orbit on a compact torus. For these companion substitutions, the required multiplicity-one Rauzy geometry is automatic: Barge's pure-discreteness theorem applies after reversal of the substitution words. The Rauzy torus also gives a prime number theorem for the substitution fixed word: every finite factor occurs at prime starting positions with its ordinary factor frequency. This proves the Tribonacci prime-number theorem suggested by Drmota--M\"ullner--Spiegelhofer. The toral model further yields polynomial sampling laws, asymptotic independence from fixed congruence classes, fixed-shift correlation formulas, and M\"obius orthogonality. Combined with established prime theorems, it gives a terminal refinement of Chebotarev and shows that every fixed terminal prime class contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions with polylogarithmically bounded common difference.

analysis.relevance_note: Substitution dynamics, Rauzy geometry, toral models, and word frequencies are directly central to symbolic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Under the stated Pisot and minimal-polynomial assumptions, terminal block words have explicit asymptotic frequencies among primes. A toral model also gives prime sampling laws for substitution words.

paper.title: Totally invariant subvarieties of $\mathbf P^n$
paper.abstract: Let $f:\mathbf P^n_{\mathbb C}\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbb C}$ be an endomorphism of degree greater than one. We prove that every irreducible Zariski closed subset $V$ with $f^{-1}(V)=V$ is a linear subspace.

analysis.relevance_note: The abstract concerns algebraic rigidity of totally invariant subvarieties, without a stated entropy, symbolic, or fractal-dimension component.

paper.title: Koopman Observers for Diffusion Acceleration: Correcting Feature Forecasts with Shallow Measurements
paper.abstract: Feature caching accelerates diffusion sampling by replacing expensive network evaluations with predictions from previously computed activations. However, forecasts based only on past features cannot directly incorporate changes in the current denoising state. We investigate whether inexpensive, freshly computed features can serve as observations for correcting these predictions. We introduce an observation-corrected Koopman framework for accelerating frozen diffusion models. Using calibration trajectories, we identify finite-dimensional, time-dependent Koopman approximations that jointly describe the increments of shallow and deep network features. During accelerated sampling, these operators predict the evolution of expensive deep features, while innovations in the observed shallow features correct the predicted state. Periodic full evaluations refresh the observer, and all generative-model parameters remain unchanged. This formulation enables controlled comparisons of temporal prediction and observation correction. Across three 10,000-image runs per dataset, our method reduces paired Inception-feature MSE by $19.9\%$ on CIFAR-10 and $11.9\%$ on a ten-class ImageNet subset relative to channelwise affine prediction under the same four-partial-step schedule. Matched ablations attribute additional reductions of $4.54\%$ and $4.67\%$ to observation correction. The observer achieves $1.89\times$ and $1.85\times$ measured speedups over DDIM-50, supporting improved reference-sampler fidelity without retraining the denoiser.

analysis.relevance_note: The work uses numerical Koopman approximations to accelerate image-generation sampling, without a central connection to the strongest mathematical interests.

paper.title: The local dynamical structure of $\Delta^*$ sets via a new Furstenberg family algebra
paper.abstract: In this paper, we strengthen the connection between the combinatorics of difference sets and the dynamics of group rotations. Our main result shows that sets which have non-empty intersection with all difference subsets of a commutative semigroup possess local Bohr structure. This generalizes results of Bergelson, Furstenberg, and Weiss and Host and Kra from the integers to arbitrary commutative semigroups. We accomplish this by A) utilizing a recent result showing that the regionally proximal relation is an equivalence relation for minimal actions of commutative semigroups and by B) describing a new, DeMorgan-type algebra on Furstenberg families that allows for efficient manipulation and computation. We formally verify all of the results in this paper in Lean. The main results are verified in a Palomar submission, and we link to a Github repository containing code for the complete verification.

paper.title: Hyperbolicity and obstructions to PL actions of the circle
paper.abstract: We prove the following ``Torus Trichotomy Theorem'': every finitely generated subgroup of $\pls$ is either virtually free, a central extension of a cocompact Fuchsian group by a finite cyclic group, or a one-ended, non-acylindrically-hyperbolic group containing $\mathbb{Z}^2$. In particular, we obtain the ``free or surface'' alternative for word-hyperbolic groups of PL homeomorphisms of the circle.

paper.title: Geometric finiteness in paracomplex hyperbolic spaces
paper.abstract: We develop a framework for studying discrete subgroups of $\mathsf{PGL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})$ via the paracomplex hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}_\tau^d$, a rank-$1$ pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space. We characterize projective transverse, relatively Anosov, and Anosov subgroups in terms of properly discontinuous, geometrically finite, and convex-cocompact actions respectively on their weak hulls, which are canonical flow spaces in the spacelike unit tangent bundle of $\mathbb{H}_\tau^d$. A key ingredient is the construction of a Busemann-type horofunction on the spacelike unit tangent bundle with the properties needed to describe cuspidal geometry. We further prove for relatively Anosov subgroups that the geodesic flows on their weak hulls are uniformly hyperbolic, giving a relative analogue of the Axiom A property.

analysis.relevance_note: Anosov group actions and uniformly hyperbolic geodesic flows provide a substantial connection to the hyperbolic and group-action interests.
analysis.tldr: Discrete projective groups admit dynamical characterizations through actions on weak hulls in paracomplex hyperbolic space. Relatively Anosov groups yield uniformly hyperbolic geodesic flows on these hulls.

These are canonical flow spaces in the spacelike unit tangent bundle of the rank-one pseudo-Riemannian space \(\mathbb{H}_\tau^d\).
